turn_text: You and Senator Heintkamp have introduced a bill that would tweak the Ag Risk Coverage County program. What are the mistakes that we saw in the 14 bill that need to be corrected now?

Well, this does strengthen and improve what we call ARK. And it does help our farmers, when those commodity prices fall, to those damaging levels. But we need to make sure that they are getting accurate payments And in Iowa, for example, 97% of our farmers corn acres and 98% of the soybean acres are enrolled in the ARK program. But unfortunately, a lot of our farmers have experienced payment discrepancies because of the program's reliance on administrative county lines rather than a farm's actual physical location. So the legislation will ensure that the data and the processes used by the FSA to determine payments, making sure that they're not unfairly affected by state or federal boundaries, that really have no bearing on a particular farm's yield. So we are excited to be able to present this. We are hoping that it's taken up by the committee, if not part of our Farm Bill package. So it's a good move. We've heard a lot of feedback on this, and we hope that this can correct some of those discrepancies.
Given the downfall that we've seen in farm income even over the life of this previous build, do you not feel like that probably farmers may be taking a harder look at the PLC in comparison to ARK?

Well, it is quite possible that they start turning that direction. We are in a challenging time right now. And so it is possible, but that means, you know, this is still okay. We need to go ahead and make the corrections to ARK as necessary to make sure that if they so choose to keep those acres in, ARK, that it is a fair outcome for them.
